name: Tlahuica de San Juan Atzingo
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.

México: El Colegio de México. 294 pp. Open access:https://repositorio.colmex.mx/concern/books/7m01bp705(PDFhttps://repositorio.colmex.mx/downloads/gq67jv41p).
catalog_locator: Fonología, sec. 1.5 'Acento y tono', p. 44; parallel statement sec. 1.3.17 'Alargamiento de vocales acentuadas', pp. 40-41; stressed example forms secs. 1.3.18-1.3.19 p. 41 and sec. 1.6 p. 44
catalog_quote: El acento principal siempre recae sobre la primera sílaba de la raíz verbal o nominal y causa un leve alargamiento vocálico que no se marca en la transcripción fonética para establecer la distinción entre las vocales largas fonémicas. Con respecto al tono, el tlahuica presenta cuatro tonos distintivos que son alto, bajo y dos de contorno ascendente y descendente: [ʔɨɨ] con tono alto significa ‘dormir’ y con tono bajo ‘encender el fuego’ En el Archivo se marca el tono alto con una tilde (´), el tono bajo no se marca y el tono ascendente con una tilde en la vocal alta del desliz.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: Primary stress always falls on the first syllable of the verbal or nominal root and causes a slight vowel lengthening, which is not marked in the phonetic transcription so as to keep the distinction from the phonemic long vowels. As for tone, Tlahuica has four distinctive tones, high, low and two contour tones, rising and falling: [ʔɨɨ] with high tone means 'to sleep' and with low tone 'to light the fire'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is morphologically determined: it falls on the first syllable of the (nominal or verbal) root, skipping the person/TAM prefixes; stressed vowels are slightly lengthened. The language is also tonal (4 tones), so this is a tone language with an explicit stress statement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described (the source speaks only of 'acento principal/primario').
new_statements.exceptions: None in Muntzel & González 2017. Martínez Ortega 2012 (pp.79-81, saved file) adds that stress tracks high/rising tone: high-toned suffixes such as plural -hnə́ and applicative -pí take the high tone and the stress off the root (tu'pó 'lo perdió' -> tupo'pí 'se lo perdió'), and prefixes are always low-toned and unstressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, stated for nominal and verbal words in a root+affix template; examples are inflected verb forms and citation nouns. Co-exists with a four-way lexical tone contrast.
new_statements.identity_note: Both saved sources describe the Tlahuica (Ocuilteco, autonym pjyekakjó) of San Juan Atzingo, municipio de Ocuilan, Estado de México, which is exactly Glottolog atzi1235 'Atzingo Matlatzinca' (ISO ocu); not to be confused with San Francisco Oxtotilpa Matlatzinca (sanf1262, ISO mat).

tone_statements.citation: Herrera Zendejas, Esther. 2015. Estructuras métricas y tono en ocuilteco. In Esther Herrera Zendejas (ed.), Tono, acento y estructuras métricas en lenguas mexicanas, 279-303. México: El Colegio de México, Centro de Estudios Lingüísticos y Literarios. ISBN 978-607-462-688-9.
tone_statements.quote: … el ocuilteco es una lengua que recurre a los cambios de la tonía para diferenciar significados; a nivel fonético tiene un tono bajo, un alto y un ascendente; este último resulta de la combinación de dos tonos: el alto y el bajo, por lo que a nivel fonológico solo los tonos de nivel son pertinentes. … los dos tonos fonológicos están restringidos a la sílaba tónica … El tono bajo no contrasta en las bases, su aparición se restringe a los prefijos … el tono ascendente requiere dos moras y el tono alto una mora.
tone_statements.translation: Ocuilteco is a language that uses pitch changes to distinguish meanings; phonetically it has a low, a high and a rising tone; the latter results from the combination of two tones, high and low, so that at the phonological level only the level tones are relevant. … the two phonological tones are restricted to the stressed syllable … The low tone does not contrast on bases; its occurrence is restricted to the prefixes … the rising tone requires two moras and the high tone one mora.
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones, high and low; roots contrast high vs rising (low+high over two moras) only in the stressed syllable, head of an iambic foot; prefixes are low; unstressed tones lowered by sandhi.

sources.citation: Martínez Ortega, Aileen Patricia. 2012. Clases verbales, transitividad y valencia verbal en el pjyekakjó, tlahuica de San Juan Atzingo. Tesis de doctorado, El Colegio de México. 328 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3, pp.79-81: cites Muntzel (1986:45) that stress always falls on the first syllable of the nominal/verbal base; author adds that intensity stress is attracted to the high or rising tone of the verbal root (person/TAM prefixes are low-toned and unstressed), and that high-toned suffixes such as plural -hnə́ and applicative -pí take the high tone and the stress away from the root (tu'pó 'lo perdió' -> tupo'pí 'se lo perdió').
